newsitem.title: JAPAN: IBJ seen cutting July long-term prime to 2.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: IBJ seen cutting July long-term prime to 2.7 pct.

text.p: The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd is likely to cut its long-term prime rate by 0.2 percentage point to 2.7 percent in July, bond traders said on Tuesday.
The IBJ is scheduled to announce its long-term prime rate later this afternoon.
The prime rate, at which long-term credit banks lend to their most creditworthy customers, was last cut by 0.2 percentage point to 2.9 percent in June.
The IBJ customarily sets its long-term prime rate 0.9 percentage point above its five-year debenture coupon rate.
IBJ's June five-year bank debentures with a coupon rate of two percent were traded at 1.8 percent on Tuesday, bond traders said.
